info.title: Munafa.io network surface
info.note: Munafa has no backend of its own (no Express server, no database, no auth). The only real HTTP endpoint the frontend talks to is a same-origin rewrite that forwards to the Yahoo Finance unofficial chart API. Watchlist, search, and comparison are client-side only (localStorage + this one endpoint) and are NOT separate server routes, so they are intentionally not listed as paths here -- an OpenAPI-style spec for them would be fictional.

get.summary: Proxied Yahoo Finance chart lookup for one NSE-listed symbol.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: NSE ticker with .NS suffix, e.g. RELIANCE.NS. No allowlist/validation happens before this reaches Yahoo.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Candle interval. The app only ever sends values from buildChartParams(), but the endpoint itself does not validate the value.

200_or_404_error.description: Symbol not recognized, or bad params. Yahoo answers with HTTP 200 or 404 (both observed) and a chart.error object rather than a 4xx body in most cases -- callers must check chart.error, not just status_code.

429.description: OBSERVED IN PRODUCTION: the /api/yahoo/* path is rate-limited by the hosting edge network independently of Yahoo's own limits. A short burst (as few as 4-5 requests within a couple of seconds) can trip it. Plain-text body 'Edge: Too Many Requests', not JSON. No documented threshold or Retry-After header.
429.shape: text/html or text/plain body, not JSON

known_issues: 429 responses are undocumented and untyped -- the frontend's fetchYahooChart() does not special-case them, so a rate-limited call surfaces as a generic fetch failure.
No caching at the edge -- stockService.js's 30s in-memory cache only protects a single browser tab; concurrent users/tabs each spend their own quota against the same rate limit.
